title: The three-party sign-in
lede: Follow the browser, your application, and an identity provider through one authorization-code sign-in.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.detail: The user agent follows redirects and holds the application session cookie.

nodes.label: Your application
nodes.detail: A confidential web client keeps the PKCE verifier and credentials on its server.

nodes.label: Identity provider
nodes.detail: Authenticates the person and issues an authorization code and tokens.

edges.label: Start sign-in
edges.detail: The browser asks the application to start an authentication transaction.

edges.label: Redirect to provider
edges.detail: The app creates transaction-bound state, nonce and a PKCE verifier; the redirect carries the S256 challenge.

edges.label: Authorize + challenge
edges.detail: The person authenticates at the provider and grants consent if required.

edges.label: Redirect with code
edges.detail: The provider returns a short-lived authorization code through the browser.

edges.label: Callback: code + state
edges.detail: The browser follows the registered callback URI with the authorization response.

edges.label: Check response binding
edges.detail: The application verifies the transaction and response binding before exchanging the code.

edges.label: Code + PKCE verifier
edges.detail: The server exchanges the code at the token endpoint using the saved verifier and its client authentication.

edges.label: ID + access tokens
edges.detail: Tokens return directly to the application server, not through the redirect.

edges.label: Validate ID token
edges.detail: Validate signature, issuer, audience, expiration and nonce. Invalid results stop sign-in.

edges.label: Create application session
edges.detail: Only after validation does the app create its own session and send a Secure, HttpOnly session cookie.

steps.title: Start at your application
steps.body: A click begins a transaction owned by the application. The browser does not send its password to your application.

steps.title: Bind this sign-in attempt
steps.body: The server stores state, nonce and the PKCE verifier. It redirects the browser with a transaction-specific S256 challenge.

steps.title: Authenticate at the provider
steps.body: The browser visits the identity provider. Authentication and consent are collapsed into this hop; they are not implemented by this page.

steps.title: Return an authorization code
steps.body: The provider redirects to the registered callback. This carries a code rather than the identity tokens.

steps.title: Deliver the callback
steps.body: The browser follows the callback URL and returns the response to the application.

steps.title: Check transaction binding
steps.body: The application validates the saved transaction and returned state. An invalid or abandoned response stops here.

steps.title: Exchange on the server
steps.body: The application sends the code and saved verifier to the token endpoint over TLS, using the appropriate client authentication.

steps.title: Receive tokens privately
steps.body: The provider returns tokens on the server connection. The browser redirect is not the token delivery channel.

steps.title: Validate identity claims
steps.body: The application verifies the ID token, including signature, issuer, audience, expiration and nonce, before trusting the identity.

steps.title: Create your own session
steps.body: With validation complete, the application establishes its session. Session expiry and logout are outside this focused example.

assumptions: “Three-party” means browser / application / provider, not the TCP three-way handshake and not three messages.
Illustrative confidential web application using OpenID Connect authorization code and S256 PKCE over TLS.
Authentication UI, failures, token renewal and logout are omitted. Arrows show message direction; redirects are browser-mediated.
This is a focused sequence view: no activation bars or combined fragments. The page demonstrates a protocol; it does not execute a login.
